title: Premium Accounting Standard: Midterm Premium Changes on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
Every midterm premium change on a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is prorated on calendar days. This standard governs how such a change is measured, how its premium entry is written, and how endorsement effective dates are set.

## Clauses in force

**1. Two ratings.** The full-term premium is rated twice under the full-term rating rule, both on the change's effective date: once as it stood the day before the change, and once as it stands with the change. The change is the difference between the two.

**2. Direction of the entry.**

| Difference (with the change, less before it) | Entry written |
|---|---|
| Positive | Additional premium |
| Negative | Return premium of the absolute amount |
| Zero | Neither |

**3. One entry per transaction.** Each additional or return premium entry carries the reference of the one transaction that produced it, so two changes on the same day produce two separate entries.

**4. Changes requested together.** Several changes requested together with the same effective date are still processed one transaction at a time. Each is rated against the premium left by the previous one.

**5. Effective date limit.** An endorsement effective date may be today, or a later date no more than the package's future-dating limit ahead. That limit is 30 calendar days on every package.

Hypothetical: a request made today may take an effective date from today through the 30th calendar day from today. A date on the 31st day is beyond the limit.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this standard are **no longer in force** and are superseded by the current basis. They are kept here only so the record of the standard is complete:

- the former clause under which the difference between the two ratings was multiplied by the unexpired days of the term divided by the days in the term and rounded to the cent (half up);
- the former clause under which an endorsement effective date could not be earlier than today, except for a newly acquired vehicle within its automatic coverage window and a driver removal for a death, which took the actual date;
- the former clause under which, for a cancellation, the return premium was the pro rata unearned premium of the written premium of the term, before any fee or minimum earned premium.

superseded_clauses: the difference is multiplied by the unexpired days of the term divided by the days in the term and rounded to the cent (half up).
it may not be earlier than today except for a newly acquired vehicle within its automatic coverage window under auto_vehicle_changes and a driver removal for a death, which take the actual date.
For a cancellation, the return premium is the pro rata unearned premium of the written premium of the term, before any fee or minimum earned premium under auto_insured_cancellation.
